title: Chinoyo
speaker: Shin-yu Scott Allen
summary: Shin-yu Scott Allen takes up Chiyono, the thirteenth-century Japanese nun credited as the first woman abbess in Japan, and a second nun at Tokeiji who meditated on Chiyono's poem. Chiyono, grieving her husband, awakens when the bottom of a mended bucket gives way and the moon's reflection drains out with the water. The second nun's poem finds the moon multiplied in every rain puddle, which leads Shin-yu to the false self and to a 7-Eleven stop where a big man in a huge pickup turns out to want only to ask about the mileage on a Toyota Yaris. Shin-yu closes by reading Dogen's passage on the original face from Shobogenzo Zuimonki twice, followed by quiet sitting and small-group discussion.
